card.name: Literary forms after writer descriptions
card.fires_on: Linking words and punctuation (and, from, to, a colon) in writer biographies, right where the next word would name a literary form such as stories, essays, prose, poetry or drama.

modes.label: Lists of genres
modes.description: A linking word inside a list of what an author wrote, just before the next genre.
modes.example: Fitzgerald (September 24, 1896 – December 21, 1940) was an American author of novels<< and>> short stories, whose works are the paradigm

modes.label: Writing verbs and roles
modes.description: Words such as write or poet and dramatist where a kind of writing comes next.
modes.example: content of his poetry. As can be seen from this anthology, his verse inspired many composers but, interestingly, he himself began to<< write>> lyrics in the 194

modes.label: Award categories
modes.description: The word for in a literary award name, before a category such as Best Novel.
modes.example: 985 Locus Award for Science Fiction novel The Integral Trees was a nominee for the following awards - 1985 Hugo Award<< for>> Best Novel - 198

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words for literary forms such as prose, poetry, screenplay and pamphlet, including Chinese terms for them.
card.plain: It fires in author biographies when the text is about to name a kind of writing, such as prose, poems or stories.
